reason: The single source of truth for all 459 v1 endpoints: the per-module method/path/purpose/token/scope tables (§3), the two auth flows (§1), pagination plus the exactly-five POST .../search endpoints (§4.1/§4.3), the error shape and the fact that only 100000/100038 are documented (§4.4), and the ENT-only 61 / USER-only 7 split (§7). Every catalog entry, every D7 command mapping and every child's endpoint list must be quoted from here — never from memory, never re-researched online.

The established module architecture this task extends: searchPaginate reuse, the --x/--x-id flag pair, metadata cache keying and parent scoping, the error map, and §14's live-verified findings (paths is the ancestor chain not the node's own path; PATCH does not reassign executor; bulk is neither atomic nor best-effort). design.md cites it as [TH§x] and deliberately does not repeat any of it.

The slice/gate pattern every F and S child follows, plus the ground rules that still bind: the forbidden core files, the single ERROR_CODE_OVERRIDES exception with one recorded observation per row, one commit per slice with typecheck+test green, and 'when live contradicts the docs, update research/ and design.md in the same commit rather than coding around it'.

Precedent for landing a whole new API domain in one milestone — exactly what S1a-S1d do with scm/build/release (three brand-new command groups). Shows the endpoints -> types -> api -> metadata -> cli slice order, the productScoped resolver factory that F4's RESOLVERS table generalises, and the search-only read-path decision now recorded at endpoints.ts:38-41.

Needed by S3: the 65-endpoint report behind the client-side bulk cap of 50, the two distinct history shapes (run side executed_status object + remark vs case side flat status string, which must never share a deserializer), and the case/run singular-vs-plural segment trap. S3 also splits the 1845-line testhub command file, so it must not re-derive these facts.

The enforced layering invariant (cli->{api,core}, api->core, core->neither; api never imports output; cli never imports node:fs nor uses buildUrl) and the 'one new endpoint = path + type + wrapper + command' rule. Its 'Layering pressure resolved correctly' note is also the precedent for why core/catalog/ is the only correct home for the generated catalog, the same reason endpoints.ts and redact.ts live in core.

The exit-code table is a public contract this task must not renumber: the generic executor's pre-flight refusals are all UsageError (2), DryRunHalt is control flow that exits 0, and an unrecognised vendor code must stay ApiError (7) rather than be reinterpreted. Also the ERROR_CODE_OVERRIDES discipline — code string only, never message text, and only for codes actually observed live — which PRD R5 restates as a per-row evidence requirement.

Forbidden patterns that directly constrain this task: never shape-validate an id client-side (catalog path params pass through untouched), never match on API message text, no new runtime dependency (so the catalog may not pull in a schema/YAML library), no real network in tests (injected fetch is how the 459-endpoint dry-run sweep must be written), and exactOptionalPropertyTypes, which dictates how CatalogEntry's optional fields are declared.

The stdout/stderr contract the generic executor lives or dies by: stdout carries only the result (here, raw JSON), everything else is stderr, and a --dry-run plan is a result printed on stdout. Also the redaction mechanism — every printable URL goes through redactUrl because client_secret travels in the query string on this API — which both the api command's dry-run plan and its catalog-derived 403 scope hint must respect.

F4 refactors core/metadata.ts, whose on-disk cache this file specifies: the sha256 (apiBase, clientId, projectId, kind) key and why dropping any component is a correctness bug, the 24 h TTL, --no-cache, and invalidate-and-retry-exactly-once. F4's acceptance is zero behaviour change, so these rules are the definition of 'unchanged'. It also settles that the catalog is a build artifact, not user state, and must not live under ~/.pingcode/.

The whole D-series design is reuse: the generic executor reuses core/http.ts and both paginate flavours instead of adding a transport path, F4 collapses ~700 lines of near-duplicate resolvers into one table, and F5 mounts a single crosscutting implementation on many parents instead of copying it per entity. 'Abstract when the same code appears 3+ times' is the test each child applies before hand-writing a new helper.

Required reading when a feature spans 3+ layers, which every S child does: endpoints.ts -> types/<module>.ts -> api/parse/<module>.ts -> api/<module>.ts -> core/metadata registry -> cli/commands/<group>. F1 splits the type and parser layers precisely so these boundaries stay separable while eight children work in parallel.

Conventional Commits, machine-enforced by npm run check:commits in CI (and against the PR title, because a squash merge takes it as the subject). It matters here because the rollback plan is built on commit boundaries: each child is one revertable unit, the generated catalog is committed separately from its hand-written loader, and S3's file split must be a separate commit from its new leaves.
